rect.title: This diagram is drawn from ply.yaml, the file describing this codebase's architecture and verification claims. Each box is a component; chips are functions with their declared checks; arrows are permitted calls (solid) and data flows (dashed); red bars are forbidden calls. A box's green depth is the strength of the checks it declares — white means something inside declares none, deeper green means stronger checks, and the weakest function sets the whole box's shade. It is a promise scale, not results: none of it has run yet. Hover anything for its meaning.

#8 marks an unresolved decision — a question the design still owes an answer: venue failover: mirror orders to a backup gateway or halt. It belongs to the workspace as a whole, not to any function or component yet; Ply tracks it until someone resolves it (§5.6).

component ingest — maps to Rust module ingest collapsed — 4 components and 7 functions folded inside; render with --depth or --focus <name> to expand no checks are declared anywhere in this component — nothing here is verified yet (unclaimed)
this component may use `net` somewhere in its folded subtree. A component may use only the capabilities it declares — using an undeclared one is an architecture finding (§5.3, A0404).
this component may use `unsafe` somewhere in its folded subtree. A component may use only the capabilities it declares — using an undeclared one is an architecture finding (§5.3, A0404).

component strategy — maps to Rust module strat declares checks up to tested — checked once against the declared examples and generated inputs — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet

component signals — maps to Rust module strat::signals pure — the double border is the seal: this component declares no capabilities and may not use any; capability use inside it is an error (A0408) declares checks up to bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet
momentum bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times fuzz(2048) — runs the function on 2048 random inputs, checking the contract on each
Strategy::on_update test — runs the declared examples plus generated inputs, checking the contract on each

component risk — maps to Rust module risk owns risk::Limits — only this component may mutate them strict — architecture findings inside this component fail the build (errors, not warnings) declares checks up to bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet

check_order bounded(3) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 3 times fuzz(4096) — runs the function on 4096 random inputs, checking the contract on each mutate — plants small deliberate bugs; the test/fuzz checks must catch every one, or the contract is flagged weak contract at the watermark: requires: order.qty > 0 && order.px > 0 ensures: |r| r.is_err() == (order.qty > limits.max_qty) the checks above test the function against exactly this promise

component oms — maps to Rust module oms owns oms::OrderStore — only this component may mutate them declares checks up to bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet
